transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. I guess what finally pushed me to come in is… I’m having a really hard time staying with things that I absolutely need to stay with at work. I manage medical and health services, so a lot of my day is EPIC reports, quality metrics, clinic performance meetings — things where the details really matter.

And I’ll sit down with every intention of focusing. Like, I’ll open an EPIC quality report and tell myself, “Okay, just track these numbers, follow the trend, pull out what matters,” and within a few minutes I realize my mind has wandered so far that I’m just staring at the same section or rereading the same numbers over and over. Or in a clinic metrics meeting, people will be discussing something important, and I’m nodding and trying to follow, but then suddenly I realize I missed the whole point of what was just said.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to be careless. I know the work, and I care about it. But it feels like my attention just slips away from me, even when I’m making a real effort. That’s the part that made me think I should probably talk to someone instead of just continuing to push through it.
Before age 12, did you already have this kind of trouble staying focused?

Yes, I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t exactly talked about the way it is now, but even in elementary school I remember that pattern being there.

Teachers would write things like that I was bright, but careless — that phrase came up more than once. And I remember feeling confused by that because I wasn’t trying to be careless. I’d know the material, but then I’d miss part of the directions or skip something on a worksheet or not finish things the way I was supposed to.

My mother had to sit with me a lot while I did homework, not because I couldn’t understand it, but because I’d lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. I’d forget assignments, or I’d leave a book I needed at school and then we’d have this whole ordeal at home because I couldn’t do the work without it. So yes, before 12, definitely — it was there, just framed more like I was scattered or not applying myself.
Do these same attention problems also show up outside of work, like at home or in everyday tasks?

Yes, it does. Work is where it’s most obvious because there are consequences and other people notice, but it’s not only there.

It’s the same kind of thing where I’ll sit down intending to focus on something at home or just in regular life, and a few minutes later I realize I’m not actually taking it in anymore. Like at work, what finally made me come in was that I can open an EPIC quality report or sit through a clinic metrics meeting fully intending to track the numbers or follow the discussion, and then suddenly I’m rereading the same numbers again and again or realizing I missed the main point of what someone was saying. That pattern feels very familiar outside work too — just less formally measured, I guess.

It’s frustrating because I’m not choosing to tune out. I’m trying to stay with it, and then my attention just kind of slips away before I even realize it happened.
Do you often feel excessive worry that is hard to control?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as excessive worry that’s hard to control. I mean, I worry about normal things — work responsibilities, whether I’m keeping up, things at home — but I don’t know that it feels like worry is the main problem or like I’m constantly consumed by it.

Sometimes I do get concerned when I’ve missed something or I’m afraid I may have dropped a ball, but that feels more like a reaction to what’s happening than this ongoing uncontrollable worry, if that makes sense. I wouldn’t say I’m someone who’s sitting there unable to stop worrying all day.
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time lately?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have moments where I feel discouraged or frustrated, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up or I’ve missed something I should have caught, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the time.

It’s more like I get upset with myself in certain situations, and then it passes or at least it doesn’t feel like this constant low mood hanging over everything. I’m not waking up every day feeling depressed, if that’s what you mean. So… no, not much of the time lately.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Not really in a major way, I don’t think. I mean, I have the usual nights where I stay up later than I should or my mind is still sort of processing the day, but I wouldn’t say sleep has been a big problem I’m coming in for.

I usually can sleep, and I haven’t really noticed a consistent pattern where I’m lying awake for hours or waking up all night. If anything, when I’m tired it feels more like I didn’t manage my evening well or I got caught up doing something too late, not like I can’t sleep. So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve been having significant trouble sleeping.
